nodes.label: ARIA — local-first Windows AI assistant
nodes.rationale: Electron UI plus Python sidecar brain; one phase implemented per session so each phase can be signed off before the next builds on it.

nodes.label: Python sidecar (the brain)
nodes.rationale: All state lives here so the renderer can be hot-reloaded, closed or replaced without losing conversation, memory or task state.

nodes.label: Electron renderer (pure view)
nodes.rationale: A pure view: it renders what it is told and owns only the devices (microphone, speakers) the sidecar cannot reach.

nodes.label: Keep the knowledge graph current
nodes.rationale: The graph goes stale the moment code changes, so refreshing it is part of finishing the work rather than something to be asked for. Refresh at the end of any session touching sidecar/, src/, electron/ or scripts/.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ (graph.json, graph.html, GRAPH_REPORT.md)
nodes.rationale: The persisted knowledge graph of the repo and its rendered outputs.

nodes.label: graphify update . (AST-only refresh)
nodes.rationale: No LLM, no API key, no tokens — seconds not minutes — so it is cheap enough to run unconditionally at the end of a session. It merges into the existing graph and leaves outputs untouched when nothing structural moved, printing 'No code-graph topology changes detected'. Safe to run when unsure.

nodes.label: update is code-only, by design
nodes.rationale: Changes to BUILD_SPEC.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md or any image are invisible to AST extraction; those need semantic extraction. The command says so itself when it finishes.

nodes.label: /graphify --update (semantic re-extraction)
nodes.rationale: Dispatches subagents to extract docs and images. Needed roughly once a phase, because this CLAUDE.md is itself in the graph and every phase edits it — exactly the case the code-only update will not pick up.

nodes.label: Graph shrink guard
nodes.rationale: Exists so a failed extraction cannot silently gut a good graph. A refactor that deletes code shrinks the graph and the guard blocks that write.

nodes.label: graphify update . --force
nodes.rationale: Only for a genuinely intended shrink after the guard blocks it. Never reach for --force to make an error go away.

nodes.label: graphify cluster-only .
nodes.rationale: Re-clusters and regenerates the report from the existing graph without re-extracting. Use when the communities look wrong but the code has not moved.

nodes.label: graphify check-update .
nodes.rationale: Reports whether a semantic re-extraction is pending; cron-safe and changes nothing.

nodes.label: Two benign extractor gaps
nodes.rationale: settings.local.json yields zero nodes and 4 .sql migration files are skipped because tree_sitter_sql is absent (pip install "graphifyy[sql]"). Neither warning is a failed update.

nodes.label: Rule 1 — all state lives in the sidecar
nodes.rationale: Never store conversation, memory or task state in React or Electron main; the renderer is a pure view.
nodes.norm_label: rule 1 — all state lives in the sidecar

nodes.label: Rule 2 — one model on the GPU, 6GB ceiling
nodes.rationale: STT, embeddings, wake word and router run on CPU only. Two models on a 6GB card does not fail cleanly — it stalls generation for minutes and reads as a hang.
nodes.norm_label: rule 2 — one model on the gpu, 6gb ceiling

nodes.label: Rule 3 — never add torch
nodes.rationale: It breaks PyInstaller packaging.

nodes.label: Rule 4 — every tool goes through the registry
nodes.rationale: sidecar/tools/registry.py with an explicit permission tier; no ad-hoc subprocess calls outside a tool.
nodes.norm_label: rule 4 — every tool goes through the registry

nodes.label: Rule 5 — destructive ops need T2+ and confirmation
nodes.rationale: Delete, overwrite, send, purchase, post all require a user confirmation round-trip. No exceptions.
nodes.norm_label: rule 5 — destructive ops need t2+ and confirmation

nodes.label: Rule 6 — all tool calls logged to tool_log
nodes.rationale: With args and result.
nodes.norm_label: rule 6 — all tool calls logged to tool_log

nodes.label: Rule 10 — do not refactor prior phases
nodes.rationale: Freezes earlier work, which is why seams (the provider interface, settings vs constants) have to be right the first time.
nodes.norm_label: rule 10 — do not refactor prior phases

nodes.label: Style — explicit over clever
nodes.rationale: This code will be debugged at 2am. Functions over ~50 lines get split. Error messages must say what to do next, not just what failed.

nodes.label: Phase 4 — the finder
nodes.rationale: open_path, search_files, open_file, search_content, find — name search, find-and-open and the semantic index.

nodes.label: Semantic file index (nomic-embed-text)
nodes.rationale: Measured gate: "the quotation I sent the banquet hall" finds doc_final_v3.txt, whose name contains none of those words.

nodes.label: num_gpu: 0 on every embedding call
nodes.rationale: Rule 2. Verified with ollama ps: nomic-embed-text 376MB 100% CPU beside qwen2.5:7b 5.1GB — both resident, generation undisturbed. 752ms cold, ~154ms per chunk after.

nodes.label: The indexer throttle is the feature
nodes.rationale: 20 files/min, paused entirely while conversation.busy or CPU over 60%. An indexer that makes the machine feel slow gets uninstalled.
nodes.norm_label: the indexer throttle is the feature

nodes.label: Bounded scan instead of Everything
nodes.rationale: Documents, Desktop, Downloads; depth- and time-limited, 163–185ms, cached 45s. A feature that does nothing until you install a second program is a poor answer to "say open cv and get my CV". The message still names Everything.

nodes.label: Filename ranking reuses tools/apps.score
nodes.rationale: A filename is the same problem as an app name. Recency is a quarter-weight tiebreaker: a newer budget_2026.xlsx must not answer "cv".

nodes.label: Filler words are stripped first
nodes.rationale: Without it "my cv" returned nothing: the model forwards the phrase, not the noun inside it.

nodes.label: AppData in the skip list hides %TEMP%
nodes.rationale: Correct, and it is why the first end-to-end probe indexed zero files.
nodes.norm_label: appdata in the skip list hides %temp%

nodes.label: Tests must set ARIA_INDEX_FILES=false
nodes.rationale: The RPC fixture runs the real lifespan, which otherwise walks the real Documents of whoever runs the suite.

nodes.label: Trusted folders
nodes.rationale: A trusted folder is trusted completely, deletion included, and recursively; nothing is trusted until it is added.

nodes.label: Trust decides whether she asks, never what is allowed
nodes.rationale: The refusals in files.py — drive roots, Windows, Program Files — are untouched by trust, and allow_danger_tools still decides whether a DANGER tool exists at all.
nodes.norm_label: trust decides whether she asks, never what is allowed

nodes.label: A call spanning trusted and untrusted still asks
nodes.rationale: Moving a file out of a trusted folder is not covered by trusting it — the destination is what matters. Mutation-checked: all → any moves a file out silently.
nodes.norm_label: a call spanning trusted and untrusted still asks

nodes.label: tool_log.approved_by (user / trust / null)
nodes.rationale: Migration 004. An audit trail that cannot tell user approval from trust approval is worth much less than one that can.

nodes.label: Approval is never by voice
nodes.rationale: A misheard "yes" would be the only thing between a file and deletion. This obliges the window to come forward on confirm.request, or hands-free dead-ends at a dialog nobody can see and the 120s timeout denies it.

nodes.label: Relative paths resolve against the named folder
nodes.rationale: Not the sidecar's working directory, which is the repo. The local model reliably emits downloads/hello.txt and that has to land in Downloads.
nodes.norm_label: relative paths resolve against the named folder

nodes.label: listener.heard logs the words, not chars=42
nodes.rationale: The same gap already fixed once for not_addressed; leaving it here made a voice bug undiagnosable.
nodes.norm_label: listener.heard logs the words, not chars=42

nodes.label: Fifteen tools is past §7.2's cap of ~12
nodes.rationale: Measured on qwen2.5:7b with all fifteen: 6/7, including correctly no tool for "what is the capital of Australia". Holds for now — relevance-based selection is next.
nodes.norm_label: fifteen tools is past §7.2's cap of ~12

nodes.label: Relevance-based tool selection (pending)
nodes.rationale: Sequenced, not skipped. Needs nomic-embed-text on the turn path.

nodes.label: kokoro-onnx TTS on CPU
nodes.rationale: Sentence-streamed; weights live in data/models/ (~340MB, not vendored). Missing weights log a warning and disable voice — they never stop the sidecar.

nodes.label: Synthesis cost: 230ms fixed + ~26ms per character
nodes.rationale: Measured end to end with Ollama generating concurrently. RTF ~0.35 alone, ~0.5 while the model streams; sustained playback stays ahead of speech.

nodes.label: FIRST_CHUNK_MAX_CHARS = 32
nodes.rationale: At 90 the opening fragment alone cost 2470ms, putting first audio at 3.5s. The 900ms gate is met only for short replies; faster first audio needs a cheaper voice model, not a bigger first chunk.

nodes.label: Reasoning is never spoken
nodes.rationale: SpeechStream reads delta.text and never delta.thinking; test_tts.py asserts it rather than assuming it.

nodes.label: Cancel emits audio.stop
nodes.rationale: Emitted before the task unwinds, or queued audio keeps talking for seconds after the stop button. Barge-in reuses it.

nodes.label: Chunks carry an index; renderer plays by index
nodes.rationale: Synthesis is dispatched per fragment so a short one can finish before a longer earlier one; scheduling on the WebAudio clock keeps sentences from seaming.
nodes.norm_label: chunks carry an index; renderer plays by index

nodes.label: She answers to "aria", decided from the transcript
nodes.rationale: openWakeWord ships six pretrained phrases and "aria" is not among them, so gating on the model would have meant answering to "hey jarvis". Cost: everything spoken near the microphone is transcribed in order to be thrown away (~450ms/utterance), never leaving the machine.
nodes.norm_label: she answers to "aria", decided from the transcript

nodes.label: WakeMode.PHRASE (default)
nodes.rationale: Needs no downloaded weights, only the VAD and the recogniser. Model mode falls back to it when weights are absent — being able to talk to her matters more than which phrase opens the conversation.

nodes.label: openWakeWord (ONNX)
nodes.rationale: Must be told inference_framework="onnx" (default tflite fails on Windows) and given explicit model paths or it downloads weights mid-conversation. Its [full] extra pulls torch (rule 3) and must never be installed. 127ms load, 1.68ms/80ms frame, 2.1% realtime.

nodes.label: Silero VAD via faster-whisper
nodes.rationale: providers/vad.py reuses the ONNX Silero model faster-whisper already bundles: no new dependency, no compiler, a neural detector rather than a GMM. 173ms load, 0.14ms/32ms frame, 0.4% realtime.

nodes.label: webrtcvad is not used and cannot be
nodes.rationale: It ships source-only and its C extension needs MSVC; pip install webrtcvad==2.0.10 fails here. Do not re-add it.
nodes.norm_label: webrtcvad is not used and cannot be

nodes.label: Hands-free is on by default
nodes.rationale: At Eyaas's explicit request: reaching for a key before speaking is the thing it exists to remove. Off-by-default on privacy grounds was overruled; the compromise is visibility — Windows indicator, a header switch reading "Listening", and turning it off persists.

nodes.label: useHandsFree (renderer hook)
nodes.rationale: The renderer must act on the persisted setting, not just read it: the sidecar remembers the answer but owns no microphone, so this opens the device when voice.listen comes back enabled.

nodes.label: voice.listen (returns the live phrase)
nodes.rationale: The UI never hardcodes the phrase — which one is live depends on the mode, and a label naming the wrong one is worse than no label.

nodes.label: Audio frames go over a JSON-RPC notification
nodes.rationale: 12.5 frames a second with a reply each would be 12.5 round-trips a second to hear "received". notify() drops frames when the socket is closed, which is correct — a frame is only useful immediately.
nodes.norm_label: audio frames go over a json-rpc notification

nodes.label: VoiceAura (amplitude canvas)
nodes.rationale: Driven by real amplitude over a getLevel() getter, not React state — sixty renders a second to move a waveform costs more than the waveform. The rAF loop is cancelled when idle. Listening and speaking differ by direction of travel (inward vs outward), not only hue; the ribbon sits 78px off the bottom or it hides behind the composer.

nodes.label: strip_wake_word
nodes.rationale: A leading wake phrase arrives in the same utterance as the question and would otherwise be sent to the model as part of it.

nodes.label: The screen overlay window
nodes.rationale: Ctrl+Space means "put the chat away", not "turn her off". Shown only when the main window is hidden — with the window open VoiceAura says the same thing and a glow around a window you are looking at is glare. Constructed at startup, not on first use, because a window plus a page load does not fit the 300ms budget.

nodes.label: backgroundThrottling: false is not sufficient
nodes.rationale: Chromium suspends renderers nobody is watching and the microphone lives in one. main.ts also appends disable-renderer-backgrounding, disable-background-timer-throttling and disable-backgrounding-occluded-windows before whenReady — appended after, they are ignored.

nodes.label: listener.frame_rate
nodes.rationale: A throttled capture goes quiet without erroring, so "is she still hearing me" is not answerable by looking at the app. Measured 12.5/s with the window hidden, identical to visible.

nodes.label: Overlay window flags are the whole risk
nodes.rationale: Verified via GetWindowLong: WS_EX_TRANSPARENT, WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW, WS_EX_NOACTIVATE, topmost, hidden until needed. A regression makes it an obstacle permanently on top of the user's work. Also no backgroundMaterial — acrylic requires transparent: false and this window needs a real alpha channel.
nodes.norm_label: overlay window flags are the whole risk

nodes.label: showInactive, never show
nodes.rationale: Showing activates, and activating a non-focusable window drops the user's caret.

nodes.label: sendToRenderer broadcasts to both windows
nodes.rationale: One conversation, two views. The overlay owns no audio: the window that does publishes level and mode at ~30Hz over aria:voice-level and sends one final zero when idle so the glow fades instead of freezing.

nodes.label: ListenerState.ARMED
nodes.rationale: Requiring the name and question in one breath answered only 12 of 80 real utterances — everyone says the name, waits, then asks. Called by name arms her for 10s; a cancellable timer falls back to WAITING because a window that never shuts is a microphone answering the room.

nodes.label: The follow-up window was removed
nodes.rationale: For 12s after an answer any speech became a turn, which is how she ends up answering a sentence meant for someone else. Every turn needs her name. Gate cases were flipped rather than deleted so the record shows it.

nodes.label: Fuzzy name matching on the first word
nodes.rationale: difflib, ≤1 edit, because base.en on a single short word is unreliable. The first letter must match — without that guard "Maria" is one edit from "aria" and every Maria in earshot wakes her.
nodes.norm_label: fuzzy name matching on the first word

nodes.label: listener.not_addressed logs the transcript
nodes.rationale: A character count made 64 dropped utterances impossible to explain. It also emits misheard, captioned dimly for 2s — silence is indistinguishable from a dead app.

nodes.label: useWakeChime
nodes.rationale: Synthesised in WebAudio. The glow says the same thing only if you happen to be looking at the screen you just spoke at.

nodes.label: Barge-in
nodes.rationale: Never worked at first: AssistantState.SPEAKING was read once and written nowhere in the sidecar, so the branch was unreachable — zero listener.barge_in events across the whole log. Depends on hardware because the microphone hears her own voice; 480ms by design (300ms sustained speech plus VAD ramp), and barge_in_enabled turns it off without touching the wake word.

nodes.label: A gate that supplies the precondition tests the mechanism, not the feature
nodes.rationale: gate_wakeword.py reported barge-in passing because the script itself called set_state(SPEAKING). Check what writes the state, not only what reads it.
nodes.norm_label: a gate that supplies the precondition tests the mechanism, not the feature

nodes.label: voice.playing (renderer reports playback)
nodes.rationale: The renderer is the only thing that knows, including the tail still playing after generation ends — exactly when someone interrupts. Listener keeps its own _playing flag rather than overloading AssistantState so the listener and UI stop competing for one field.

nodes.label: Duck first, decide after
nodes.rationale: Confirming "stop" needs a whole utterance plus transcription, over a second with her still talking. Sustained speech drops playback to 20% immediately (audio.duck); a false alarm costs a dip that comes back rather than a lost sentence, and ducking helps the microphone hear the speaker while it decides.

nodes.label: Only her name or a stop word cuts her off
nodes.rationale: Chosen over "any speech" because her own voice reaches the microphone through the speakers. Stop words match the whole utterance, so "stop by the shop later" is a sentence. A bare stop word sends no turn — "stop" is not a question.
nodes.norm_label: only her name or a stop word cuts her off

nodes.label: A duck must always resume (_unduck)
nodes.rationale: set_playing(False) used to clear the flag with no event, leaving the renderer's gain node at 20% for that answer and every one after — 13 ducks, 0 resumes in one log. _unduck() is the single exit and useAudio also resets gain on a new answer.

nodes.label: Whisper recognition is serialised
nodes.rationale: _lock guarded start() only, so every utterance in the room began its own thread and they fought each other, Ollama and Kokoro for cores — the entire p90 (5244ms) and max (34.3s). Utterances queued behind a newer one are dropped; an old one is almost always room noise nobody awaits.

nodes.label: base.en over tiny.en
nodes.source_location: ### She could not hear her own name
nodes.rationale: tiny.en won on synthesised speech (307ms vs 528ms median) and was reverted: its accuracy win was measured on one synthesised voice, and a corpus of one speaker cannot measure a wake word. ARIA_STT_MODEL overrides it. The synthetic gate can no longer separate the models (both 36/36) — it is a floor, not a verdict; the live log chose base.en.

nodes.label: hotwords="Aria" makes it worse, measured
nodes.source_location: ### She could not hear her own name
nodes.rationale: 24/36 with it against 32/36 without, plus a false wake. Biasing the decoder makes it treat a leading name as context already given and drop it, and it turned "Ah, yeah" into "Aria". Adding "hay" as a greeting variant fixed the last miss ("Hay Area"): both models then score 36/36 with 0 false wakes.

nodes.label: The wake check reads only the opening of long utterances
nodes.rationale: The name is the first word, so a long stretch of room speech no longer gets transcribed in full purely to be thrown away. Short requests still transcribe once — paying twice would add ~300ms to the path the user is waiting on.
nodes.norm_label: the wake check reads only the opening of long utterances

nodes.label: Esc stops her, claimed only while she speaks
nodes.rationale: Saying "stop" cannot beat 500ms of silence plus recognition; a key can. A global Space was asked for and rejected — it is swallowed mid-word in whatever you are typing.
nodes.norm_label: esc stops her, claimed only while she speaks

nodes.label: Two trailing-silence thresholds
nodes.rationale: Scanning the room needs only an utterance boundary (500ms), but somebody composing a question pauses to think — cutting them off there is what makes her feel absent, so an armed capture allows 1100ms (ARMED_TRAILING_SILENCE_MS).

nodes.label: _rearm() — a false start must not disarm her
nodes.rationale: A cough after "Aria" used to open a capture, produce nothing and drop to WAITING with the window gone, so the question needed a second "Aria". _rearm() restores the window with whatever time is left.
nodes.norm_label: _rearm() — a false start must not disarm her

nodes.label: Blue means she is listening to you
nodes.rationale: _begin_capture set LISTENING on every speculative capture, so the rim lit for any noise and went out — saying "I heard you" to someone about to be ignored. It is set only once the name is confirmed, or when the wake model fires.
nodes.norm_label: blue means she is listening to you

nodes.label: Phase 3 — the tool contract
nodes.rationale: Six tools, one per tier boundary: list_windows, get_system_info (T0), open_app, set_volume (T1), move_file (T2), delete_file (T3).

nodes.label: A confirmation timeout resolves to DENIED
nodes.rationale: Somebody who walked away has not agreed to anything. Mutation-checked: flipping that one return fails four tests and logs tool.ran ok=True tier=3 tool=obliterate.
nodes.norm_label: a confirmation timeout resolves to denied

nodes.label: DANGER tools are off by default and absent from schemas()
nodes.rationale: The model is not told those tools exist, which is stronger than asking it not to use them.
nodes.norm_label: danger tools are off by default and absent from schemas()

nodes.label: Schemas derived from type hints and docstrings
nodes.rationale: Never written twice. ctx is excluded — offered as a field, models try to fill it.
nodes.norm_label: schemas derived from type hints and docstrings

nodes.label: Only summary goes back into the context
nodes.rationale: Never data or display. §7.2 names pasting tool output into the prompt as the #2 failure mode.
nodes.norm_label: only summary goes back into the context

nodes.label: The continuation pass is not offered tools again
nodes.rationale: One tool per turn until Phase 6; a model handed its own tools straight after using one will loop. Extra calls in a single response are dropped and the model is told so.
nodes.norm_label: the continuation pass is not offered tools again

nodes.label: pycaw's GetSpeakers() API changed
nodes.rationale: It returns a wrapper with .EndpointVolume, so every Activate(IID, CLSCTX_ALL, None) example online now fails with 'AudioDevice' object has no attribute 'Activate'.

nodes.label: registry.clear() needs snapshot/restore in tests
nodes.rationale: A bare clear left the real tools missing for every later test — passed alone, failed in the run.

nodes.label: Cloud providers call tools too
nodes.rationale: They were built accepting-and-ignoring tools, so she told Eyaas "I cannot check the running processes" while routed to Gemini Flash Lite. Denying a capability she has is worse than not having it. OpenAI streams tool calls in fragments (accumulated and emitted whole); Gemini nests one tools entry holding every functionDeclarations.

nodes.label: A tool turn is not a text turn
nodes.rationale: She opened WhatsApp and said "I cannot open WhatsApp directly": Gemini received the tool call as an empty model turn and the result as a plain user message. Gemini needs functionCall/functionResponse parts with an object response; OpenAI needs type: "function", an id, and arguments as a JSON string where Ollama wants an object — one shared to_wire cannot serve both.
nodes.norm_label: a tool turn is not a text turn

nodes.label: Gemini requires thoughtSignature echoed back
nodes.rationale: Otherwise it rejects the follow-up outright. ToolCall.signature carries it opaquely for every provider.

nodes.label: _GROUNDING_TEMPLATE / stable_prefix(has_tools=...)
nodes.rationale: The prompt has two capability paragraphs and using the wrong one is visible: she opened Calculator then said she could not run programs. Only that paragraph changed — the rest of the block took qwen2.5:7b from 57% to 27% fabrication, so the anti-invention clauses stay. Both variants resolve at import so the KV prefix stays constant.

nodes.label: open_app
nodes.rationale: os.startfile only finds PATH; Notion, Calendar and most Store or Electron apps have no executable anywhere. Falls back to Get-StartApps and launches via explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\<AppID>.

nodes.label: App index: Get-StartApps + App Paths + PATH
nodes.rationale: 214 + 42 entries plus PATH, merged and cached; a miss refreshes once in case the app was installed since. Each entry carries how to launch it, because the three need different launchers.
nodes.norm_label: app index: get-startapps + app paths + path

nodes.label: open_app's ordered match bands
nodes.rationale: Exact, shared words, prefix, substring, run-together spelling, edit distance last — ordered by how badly each can go wrong. Measured 29/29 against 20/24 for the if-ladder it replaced. Help/Uninstall entries are demoted unless asked for; exact beats fuzzy so "youtube" opens the site and "youtube music" the app.

nodes.label: MATCH_FLOOR
nodes.rationale: What stops nonsense resolving to something. Opening the wrong app is worse than opening nothing. A miss names the closest three so the model or user can retry.

nodes.label: _ALIASES is a fallback, never a rewrite
nodes.rationale: It used to replace the query before matching, so "terminal" became "wt" and the real Terminal entry was never considered — an alias could make matching worse.
nodes.norm_label: _aliases is a fallback, never a rewrite

nodes.label: scripts/eval_quality.py
nodes.rationale: Two mechanical suites — no model grades another model. Run before and after any prompt, persona or model change.

nodes.label: scripts/soak_conversation.py (30-turn soak)
nodes.rationale: Clean on both local models; the Phase 1 failure (an invented rotting roof referenced for 25 turns) does not reproduce.

nodes.label: Read fabricated and over-refused together
nodes.rationale: A model that invents nothing because it refuses everything has been broken, not fixed. The grounded category is the control group and must stay at 100%.

nodes.label: An aggregate over single-turn probes is not a conversation
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: PREFERRED_LOCAL was briefly qwen3.5:4b on a 92%-vs-79% score; ten turns of real conversation reversed it (the 4B invented that Einstein never won the Nobel). The check passed the fabrication because it matched the substring "was not" — it tested the shape of a correction, not the fact.
nodes.norm_label: an aggregate over single-turn probes is not a conversation

nodes.label: The checks lie before the model does
nodes.rationale: GPT-5's U+2019 apostrophe scored a perfect refusal as 78% fabrication until probes.normalise() folded punctuation; premise probes need Expect.CORRECTION and are excluded from over-refusal; reasoning tokens count against max_tokens so GPT-5 returned empty strings; OpenAI's quota error does not contain "429" — detect ProviderRateLimited.
nodes.norm_label: the checks lie before the model does

nodes.label: Persona is per model; MINIMAL is not a downgrade
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: Over 8 runs FULL made qwen2.5:7b invent a breakfast every time; MINIMAL declined every time. Do not raise a model's level without re-running --category honesty several times.
nodes.norm_label: persona is per model; minimal is not a downgrade

nodes.label: Temperature does nothing for hallucination
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: Swept 0.0/0.3/0.8: the 7B scored 57/57/54%, the 4B 16/30/16% — flat within noise. ModelInfo carries the field, unset. Do not re-litigate without new evidence.

nodes.label: Never set temperature on a reasoning model
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: GPT-5, GPT-5 mini and the Gemini Pro preview reject any value but their default, and openai.py forwards whatever it is given. test_catalog.py guards this.
nodes.norm_label: never set temperature on a reasoning model

nodes.label: Switching local models evicts the old one first
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: OllamaProvider.unload. keep_alive=30m plus a 6GB card means two models do not fit; measured, it does not fail cleanly — it stalls generation for minutes and reads as a hang.
nodes.norm_label: switching local models evicts the old one first

nodes.label: Smart-mode bias is a persisted setting
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: fastest / balanced / quality (default), not a constant — later phases flip the setting rather than editing the router, which rule 10 freezes.
nodes.norm_label: smart-mode bias is a persisted setting

nodes.label: send() with no session_id continues the latest session
nodes.source_location: ### The battery picked the wrong model
nodes.rationale: It used to mint a new one per call, so any client that forgot to echo the id back lost all context one turn at a time. chat.new is the only way to start fresh.
nodes.norm_label: send() with no session_id continues the latest session

nodes.label: context.machine_context()
nodes.rationale: Injects date, time, answering model, session age and connectivity — facts the process already holds, no query on the turn path. Rendered to the minute, never the second: this block sits before the conversation, so a per-second string would invalidate the KV cache for every later turn (~1s). Measured 292–387ms on turns 2+.

nodes.label: providers/connectivity.py
nodes.rationale: Caches reachability on a 60s timer so she can tell "I have no web tool" from "you are offline". Reads never touch the network — probing per turn would put a round-trip in front of every reply.

nodes.label: Being reached over the internet is not having internet
nodes.rationale: The OpenAI and Gemini APIs are text-in/text-out: no browsing, no live prices, no clock. A cloud model fails "what is the Bitcoin price" for the same reason the local one does. Live data is Phase 7's research(query).
nodes.norm_label: being reached over the internet is not having internet

nodes.label: A refusal names the limit once, then points somewhere
nodes.rationale: "I cannot check the current price of Bitcoin." is true and worth nothing. The helpful-refusal category enforces this; both local models pass 4/4.
nodes.norm_label: a refusal names the limit once, then points somewhere

nodes.label: Closed: TTFT does not scale with conversation length
nodes.rationale: Median 483ms, p95 611ms over a real 30-turn conversation; growth +0.03ms per token. The old blocker was measured on qwen3.5:4b, a reasoning model paying for reasoning every turn.
nodes.norm_label: closed: ttft does not scale with conversation length

nodes.label: Stable-first prompt assembly and the KV cache
nodes.rationale: Identity, voice, boundaries and tool schemas go before anything that changes per turn; Ollama caches the KV for an unchanged prefix — worth ~1s/turn. Affect, temporal context and retrieved facts go last. Measure turn 2, not turn 1: cache-busting is invisible on a first turn.
nodes.norm_label: stable-first prompt assembly and the kv cache

nodes.label: Prefill costs ~480ms per 1000 tokens here
nodes.rationale: Over 3× what BUILD_SPEC §10 assumed, so the pre-conversation budget is ~800 tokens on local, not 2000. Bites in Phase 3 (tool schemas) and Phase 5 (retrieval).

nodes.label: Roll-up (_summarize / _maybe_roll_up) runs in the background
nodes.rationale: The remaining latency cliff is roll-up, not length. It used to run inline on the turn that crossed the budget; the turn that triggers it must not be the turn that pays for it. Voice has a ~1000ms end-to-end budget and a second model call does not fit.

nodes.label: Provider strategy — OpenAI and Gemini, not Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Supersedes BUILD_SPEC §4/§9.7. Ollama is the offline/no-key fallback, not merely the cheap path. One module per cloud vendor behind a shared interface; the Phase 1 Ollama client was designed against it from the start because rule 10 forbids refactoring later. The UI route indicator must name the provider, not just "cloud".
nodes.norm_label: provider strategy — openai and gemini, not anthropic

nodes.label: core/router.py
nodes.rationale: Picks a provider, not just local-vs-cloud.

nodes.label: Keys in Windows Credential Manager via keyring
nodes.rationale: Never .env. Done in Phase 1.5.
nodes.norm_label: keys in windows credential manager via keyring

nodes.label: Cloud vendors reached over httpx, not their SDKs
nodes.rationale: openai and google-genai are deliberately not in requirements.txt — two fewer dependency trees to survive PyInstaller.
nodes.norm_label: cloud vendors reached over httpx, not their sdks

nodes.label: qwen2.5:7b (local default)
nodes.rationale: 24% fabricated, 111/124 overall, 340ms TTFT. Its weakness is narrow — it describes non-existent packages and CLI flags as real. Ollama's tag already is 7.6B/Q4_K_M; the catalog previously said qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_K_M, which ollama list never reports, so it was greyed out as not pulled while sitting on disk.

nodes.label: qwen3.5:4b
nodes.rationale: Scored 0% fabricated on the battery but was rejected on transcripts: it invents fluently, hedges settled facts into mush, and recites its own system prompt mid-refusal. Also a reasoning model, so it pays for reasoning every turn. qwen3.5:9b is 6.6GB and cannot stay resident on a 6GB card.

nodes.label: Always send "think": false to Ollama
nodes.rationale: qwen3.5 streams into message.thinking and leaves message.content empty until reasoning ends — measured zero content tokens in 200 tokens / ~6s. Read message.content, never thinking; the TTS sentence buffer keys off content.

nodes.label: Python 3.11 in .venv, resolved by sidecar.ts
nodes.rationale: ARIA_PYTHON env, then .venv\Scripts\python.exe, then bare python. The venv launcher spawns the base interpreter as a child on Windows, so the logged pid names …\Python311\ — normal, site-packages still resolve to the venv.

nodes.label: ARIA_TOKEN handshake
nodes.rationale: Flows Electron → sidecar via env, not sidecar → file → Electron as §7.1 describes, to avoid a stale-token race on restart. The sidecar still writes data/.handshake for standalone runs.

nodes.label: system.health
nodes.rationale: Returns every §9.6 field; unprobed ones are null and named in pending_probes. Fill in your phase's probe, do not change the shape.

nodes.label: @method("name") in rpc/handlers.py
nodes.rationale: Unregistered methods return -32601 rather than a stub.

nodes.label: sidecar.log and sidecar.out.log
nodes.rationale: sidecar.log is structlog JSON from inside Python; sidecar.out.log is the child's raw stdout/stderr captured by Electron.

nodes.label: Vite hot-reloads the renderer; the sidecar is spawned once
nodes.rationale: Python edits need "Restart Brain" in the tray. A new method landing as "Unknown method 'x'. Available in this build: …" is the old process answering, not a registration bug — sidecar.ready logs the method list at startup.
nodes.norm_label: vite hot-reloads the renderer; the sidecar is spawned once
